assumptions: 'Success rate' means attempt-level success rate: successful attempts divided by all attempts, with each retry counted as a separate attempt. Order-level and technical rates are shown alongside.
The period analysed is 18-31 Oct 2026 compared with 4-17 Oct 2026, the immediately preceding period of equal length.
caveats: Duplicate records on 12 Oct: 341 attempts were ingested twice (11,704 raw rows vs 11,363 unique attempts, +3.0%). Paysight counts each attempt once and keeps the first ingestion, so figures here are de-duplicated.
Attempt volume from 18 Oct to 31 Oct was 39% above the usual level for those weekdays. This can reflect a real sale or a data gap, so be careful comparing totals across this period.
Success rate depends on the denominator: for 18-31 Oct it is 88.5% by attempts, 90.9% by orders and 92.1% on a technical basis. Retries and customer drop-offs explain the gap.
Failure codes are quoted per 100 attempts, not as shares of failures.
Mix and rate effects are split using payment method as the lens; splitting by merchant group would give different mix/rate proportions.

facts.text: Attempt success rate fell 1.47pp from 90.0% (148,791 of 165,297 attempts) to 88.5% (203,741 of 230,100 attempts). The change is statistically and practically significant.
By payment method, the split is -1.00pp from mix (shifts in share) and -0.47pp from rate (within-method changes); mix is 68.0% of the change.

CARD_EMI grew from 2.9% to 10.9% of attempts while its own rate stayed flat (81.7% to 81.6%), contributing -0.62pp. UPI's share fell from 54.0% to 42.5% at a steady rate of about 93.0%, contributing -0.44pp.
NovaMart's share of attempts rose from 6.0% to 30.0%, and its rate fell from 90.0% to 86.2%. NovaMart accounts for -0.96pp (65%) of the -1.47pp change.
Among payment methods, only DEBIT_CARD shows a significant like-for-like drop: 86.0% to 83.4% (-2.65pp). Other methods show no significant change.
Harbor Bank debit cards fell from 86.2% to 76.7% (-9.44pp), contributing -0.39pp, the largest single rate-effect segment.
For Harbor Bank debit cards, ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE rose from 0.32 to 11.12 per 100 attempts (22 to 1,065 failures). No other failure code moved by more than about 0.3 per 100 attempts.
Across all attempts, ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE rose from 0.16 to 0.71 per 100 attempts, AUTH_3DS_ABANDONED from 0.66 to 1.08, and EMI_NOT_ELIGIBLE from 0.14 to 0.50.
Overall attempt volume was 39% above the usual level for these weekdays from 18 Oct to 31 Oct.

response.headline: Attempt success rate fell 1.47pp, from 90.0% to 88.5%. About two-thirds of that (-1.00pp) is a mix shift toward lower-success payment methods (mainly card EMI) driven by NovaMart's surge in volume, and the remaining -0.47pp is a like-for-like drop concentrated in Harbor Bank debit cards.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Check NovaMart's payment-method mix by day and confirm the timing of any campaign or EMI offer against the volume spike starting 18 Oct.
hypotheses.rationale: NovaMart's share jumped from 6.0% to 30.0% at the same time as CARD_EMI share rose from 2.9% to 10.9% and overall volume spiked 39%, while EMI's own rate was flat.
hypotheses.text: A sale or campaign at NovaMart pushed a large volume of EMI-heavy traffic, which lowered the blended success rate through mix rather than because any method got worse.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Ask Harbor Bank whether risk rules or thresholds changed, and compare the risk-decline rate for NovaMart vs other merchants within Harbor Bank debit.
hypotheses.rationale: Harbor Bank debit-card risk declines went from 0.32 to 11.12 per 100 attempts, which explains most of the 9.4pp rate drop in that segment.
hypotheses.text: Harbor Bank tightened its risk rules for debit cards (or the new traffic looks riskier to it), producing a sharp rise in risk declines.

hypotheses.how_to_verify: Break NovaMart's attempts down by issuer and payment method and compare each cell's rate against the baseline period.
hypotheses.rationale: NovaMart is the top merchant driver and the Harbor Bank and EMI segments grew in the same period, but the evidence does not cross these dimensions directly.
hypotheses.text: Part of the NovaMart rate decline (90.0% to 86.2%) may be due to its mix of issuers and methods, such as Harbor Bank debit and EMI, rather than a problem specific to NovaMart.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: Harbor Bank tightened its risk rules for debit cards (or the new traffic looks riskier to it), producing a sharp rise in risk declines.
recommendations.rationale: This is the largest like-for-like drop (-9.44pp) and is driven by a single failure code.
recommendations.text: Open a risk-rule review with Harbor Bank on debit-card declines since 18 Oct, sharing the ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE spike.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: A sale or campaign at NovaMart pushed a large volume of EMI-heavy traffic, which lowered the blended success rate through mix rather than because any method got worse.
recommendations.rationale: About two-thirds of the drop is mix, which may not need a fix but should be explained and monitored.
recommendations.text: Confirm with the NovaMart account team what promotion or EMI offer started around 18 Oct, and treat the mix effect as expected if it is a planned sale.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: CARD_EMI grew from 2.9% to 10.9% of attempts while its own rate stayed flat (81.7% to 81.6%), contributing -0.62pp. UPI's share fell from 54.0% to 42.5% at a steady rate of about 93.0%, contributing -0.44pp.
recommendations.rationale: The blended rate fell 1.47pp even though most methods, including EMI and UPI, held steady.
recommendations.text: Report success rate by payment method and by merchant group alongside the blended number during the sale period, so mix shifts are not read as performance declines.

recommendations.linked_fact_or_hypothesis: Across all attempts, ISSUER_RISK_DECLINE rose from 0.16 to 0.71 per 100 attempts, AUTH_3DS_ABANDONED from 0.66 to 1.08, and EMI_NOT_ELIGIBLE from 0.14 to 0.50.
recommendations.rationale: Both rose across all traffic (AUTH_3DS_ABANDONED 0.66 to 1.08, EMI_NOT_ELIGIBLE 0.14 to 0.50 per 100 attempts) and may point to checkout friction on EMI flows.
recommendations.text: Look into the rise in 3DS abandonment and EMI eligibility failures as a secondary item.
